claims.text: Applying laser shock peening to damaged nickel-based superalloy components produces a nanocrystalline surface layer.
Laser shock peening produces high compressive residual stresses in the treated surface and subsurface.
Laser shock peening delays hot-crack initiation relative to fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Laser shock peening enhances wear resistance relative to fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Laser shock peening enhances corrosion resistance relative to fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Traditional fusion-welding repair of the specified nickel-based superalloy components is prone to hot cracking because of its high heat input.
High-intensity laser pulses generate shock waves in the treated material.
The laser-generated shock waves induce severe plastic deformation at the surface.
Shock-induced plastic deformation refines the surface grains.
The compressive residual-stress field offsets tensile stresses experienced during service.
The compressive residual-stress field hinders crack nucleation.
The compressive residual-stress field hinders crack propagation.
The proposed laser shock peening treatment improves surface hardness.
Room-temperature, rapid-pulse laser shock peening limits heat input.
Overlapping impact zones uniformly induce subsurface compressive residual stresses.
The proposed treatment induces subsurface compressive stresses without altering bulk properties.
The treatment remains effective in aggressive service environments only while the induced compressive stresses are maintained and deleterious thermal embrittlement is avoided.
